key_insight: Spatial-Agent grounds LLM-driven geospatial reasoning in formal spatial information science, reframing geo-analytical QA as explicit concept transformations so the agent computes spatial relationships instead of hallucinating them.
problem_solved: Addresses LLM agents' inability to perform reliable geospatial computation — they often rely on web search or pattern matching and hallucinate spatial relations rather than executing verifiable spatial analyses.
method: Formalize geo-analytical question answering as concept transformations using scientific core concepts from spatial information science (e.g., objects, fields, topology, metrics).
Use a hybrid agent pipeline that combines LLM-driven interpretation with symbolic/geospatial operators and explicit grounding to GIS computations to produce verifiable spatial outputs.
Evaluate on geospatial tasks and benchmarks to demonstrate reduced hallucination and improved correctness of spatial relationships and measurements.
impact: Enables reliable, verifiable geospatial reasoning in AI agents for urban analytics, transportation planning, and disaster response — reducing hallucinations and making outputs actionable for practitioners and domain experts.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user query → concept transformation layer (core spatial concepts) → symbolic/geospatial operators → verified map result

paper_title: Spatial-Agent: Agentic Geo-spatial Reasoning with Scientific Core Concepts
paper_authors: Riyang Bao, Cheng Yang, Dazhou Yu, Zhexiang Tang, Gengchen Mai
